newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares suffer correction after record days.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares suffer correction after record days.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower in a becalmed holiday market on Monday taking a breather after seven consecutive trading days of record index rises, with dealers seeing more correction ahead.

"It has been utterly calm here today and Tuesday looks like being the same on top of the recent spate of record advances and due to the school winter holidays and the absence of decision makers," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index lost 0.43 point to 152.47 in overall bourse turnover of 1.243 billion crowns.
The KFX March future rose 0.30 point to 151.90 with 143 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Top banks were again focus with a Reuters poll showing analysts predicting lower 1996 profits, when results start coming in later on in the month.
Den Danske Bank shed six crowns to finish at 563, while rival Unidanmark fell three crowns to 352.
